author: Donnell Coley
title: ECU softball will host American conference tourney - NewsBreak
text:
By Donnell Coley ,
5 hours ago
Anna Sawyer was greeted with a round of applause Sunday as she walked off the field at Max R. Joyner Family Stadium.
The East Carolina softball standout celebrated a 5-2 home win over UTSA on Senior Day. But the curtain call won’t be her final, as ECU (32-24, 16-11 American) gets set to host the 2026 American Conference Softball Championship.
Sawyer, a Greenville native, saw tons of friends, family and local youth players cheering for her team Sunday. And she hopes to see the same faces as the Pirates chase their first-ever American title when tournament action begins Wednesday.
“The whole reason I came here was just to be a small part in making the program better,” the D.H. Conley High alum said after hitting a homer to help sweep UTSA . “I feel like, over this season … I saw that come together. And I’m just so happy.”
Sawyer represents a class that has certainly turned things around and helped ECU become a contender. This season the Pirates set a new record for league victories and enter the tournament with a record-high No. 3 seed and a bye to the quarterfinals.
That’s what Shane Winkler had set out to accomplish ahead of his fifth season as ECU skipper. Though adversity came early, including losing his top power hitter in Sarah Stone, the Pirates closed their regular season with three straight series wins.
“Just really proud of this group … for everything we’ve done (during) conference (play),” Winkler said after ECU’s first sweep of the year. “We’ve had to deal with a lot through injuries and everything, but we put together a really great, solid conference season.”
That league record includes series wins over South Florida and Wichita State, the American’s No. 1 and 2 seeds, respectively.
“We’re the only team that took series (victories) from USF and Wichita … We don’t score in bunches like we have in previous years, but we find a way,” Winkler said.
His club finished eighth out of 10 American teams in hitting, and dead last in home runs after leading the league in that category a year ago.
But the Pirates, led by ace Julia Apostolakos’ 17 wins and 118 strikeouts, rank third in overall pitching.
“We feel like we’ve got a pitching staff that’s better than anyone in the league. So, you have that and a defense that takes care of it, you’re going to be in every single game. And now, it’s our hitters having confidence that we can get the big hit when it’s needed.”
The American tournament runs Wednesday through Saturday. ECU last year made it to the semifinals before losing to eventual champ USF.
Sawyer thinks the difference-maker this time around could be her team riding confidence from the month leading into tourney play.
“We’ve been rolling and I think now we just know we can beat any team, it doesn’t matter who we’re playing against,” she said. “As long as we show up that day, that’s all that matters.”
The Pirates are slated to begin tournament play on Thursday at 2:30 p.m. Championship Saturday begins at noon, with national coverage available on ESPN2.
